data.name: Time Gap
data.detailed_description:
O maior mistério do mundo está esperando por você. Somente você pode resolver o segredo do desaparecimento repentino da humanidade. Os espíritos das maiores pessoas da história humana estão lá para ajudá-lo. Explore locais vívidos por toda a Terra, desvendar o mistério, conduzir sua própria investigação!

Imagine um dia ensolarado e um café parisiense aconchegante. Pessoas andando por aí, tomando café e rindo. De repente, um flash brilhante apaga toda a vida na Terra. Não há alma por perto, mas casas vazias e ruas desertas. Tudo permanece como estava, mas as pessoas se foram. O que aconteceu e onde a humanidade desapareceu? Como personagem principal, você tem que resolver o mistério e salvar o mundo!

Durante o jogo, você descobrirá fatos curiosos sobre Alexandre, o Grande, Cleópatra, Napoleão, Lincoln e Einstein enquanto tenta salvar o dia. Viaje pelo mundo com a ajuda de um mapa interativo, conclua várias tarefas, monte diversas coleções e participe de vários minijogos. É hora de desafiar o destino!

Características:
- Complete inúmeras tarefas e jogue por meses;
- Encontre a tempestade de fogo no mapa e jogue o emocionante mini-jogo Bubble Shooter;
- Mini-jogo de sinuca está disponível! Limpe o campo para superar o furacão;
- Comece a lutar com a tempestade para jogar o mini-jogo Match 3;
- Tente a sua sorte nos cassinos de Cleópatra e Einstein a qualquer momento;
- Atenção! OVNI chegou à Terra! Encontre no mapa;
- Experimente diversas jogadas de objetos escondidos;
- Descubra fatos interessantes sobre as personalidades destacadas.

A era das maravilhas!
Seguindo a história, você viajará pelo mundo e explorará vários locais de objetos escondidos. Assim, você aumenta o seu nível de habilidade e ganha experiência para desbloquear mais locais no mapa interativo. Várias anomalias e desastres naturais diversificam a jogabilidade; portanto, às vezes você terá que completar as cenas dos objetos escondidos na escuridão total ou enfrentar a lista de itens com letras mistas. Não ceda ao desespero - todos os tipos de aprimoramentos e dicas permitirão lidar com qualquer problema que estiver no seu caminho!

Ao vasculhar cenas de objetos escondidos, você também encontrará vários itens colecionáveis ​​e especiais. Eles são necessários para atender às solicitações dos espectros de personalidades históricas que o guiarão nessa emocionante aventura. Seu diário acompanhará todas as tarefas fornecidas, pois pode haver várias delas ao mesmo tempo. Verifique regularmente e aprenda fatos interessantes sobre seus companheiros assombrados e informações importantes sobre a história do jogo para finalmente devolver a Terra à humanidade.

reviews.review:
Time Gap is a casual hidden object adventure that mixes a mystery story with a bunch of different puzzle games. I am trying to work out why humanity has suddenly disappeared while travelling between different locations on an interactive map. Along the way I meet strange ghostly characters, collect items, complete tasks and slowly uncover more of the story. It is a fairly unusual combination because I am not just doing hidden object scenes from start to finish. There are also Match 3 puzzles, Bubble Shooter sections and even a Snooker mini game.

The hidden object scenes are the part I spend most of my time with. I have to search through detailed locations and find a list of objects, but the game changes things around enough that I cannot always just scan the screen in the same way. Some scenes can be made darker, while others can mix up the letters in the item list, which makes familiar locations more difficult. I like these little changes because they stop the main puzzle from becoming completely automatic. There are also power ups that can help when I am struggling to spot something.

I also like the strange way the story brings historical figures into everything. I can learn facts about people such as Alexander the Great, Cleopatra, Napoleon, Abraham Lincoln and Albert Einstein while trying to solve the mystery. The alternate history setting gives the game more personality than I expected, and travelling around the world through the map gives me a sense that I am slowly opening up a much bigger mystery. The different locations also give me a reason to keep increasing my skill level so I can unlock more areas.

The extra mini games are useful because they break up the hidden object sections. The Match 3 game gives me something more straightforward when I want a change of pace, while the Bubble Shooter sections are quick and easy to understand. There is also a Snooker mini game that I can access from the world map, which is such a random addition that I actually find it quite amusing. There are more than 100 levels across the Match 3, Bubble Shooter and Snooker games, so there is quite a bit of extra content sitting alongside the main adventure.

The biggest problem for me is the free to play structure. Time Gap uses energy and other resources to control how much I can do, so there are times when I have to stop and wait before I can continue properly. There are also in game purchases, which can make the progression feel slower than I would like. I understand why this sort of system exists in a game built around repeated short sessions, but it can get frustrating when I am actually interested in the story and just want to keep playing.

I also think the sheer amount of tasks can become a little overwhelming. I can have several objectives active at once, along with collections to complete, locations to unlock and different events or activities appearing on the map. I like having lots to work towards, but sometimes it feels like I am managing a list of small jobs rather than following one clear adventure. The game has also received newer content and refreshed hidden object locations, which gives me more things to explore, but it makes the overall experience feel even larger and more spread out.

Overall, Time Gap is a surprisingly packed hidden object game that gives me a lot more to do than I expected. I enjoy searching through the locations, following the mystery and learning about the historical characters, while the extra puzzle games give me enough variety to stop the main gameplay from becoming too repetitive. The energy system and free to play mechanics are easily my biggest complaints, but if I treat it as a casual game that I dip into regularly rather than trying to rush through everything, I think it works quite well. It is colourful, strange and packed with little activities, and I can see myself spending a good amount of time exploring everything it has to offer.

Rating: 7.6/10
